subject: S-02
question: what "currency" takes its value per
reading: A reading: the question is what the currency a store sells in takes its value per. A market's own currency (Salla S02-V-676, Zid S02-V-751, Shopify S02-V-600, BigCommerce per storefront S02-V-809) and the buyer's (WooCommerce under WooPayments, S02-V-894) are CM-MKS-006's thing; the store's one currency, set from the store's own country on Zid, Shopify and WooCommerce (S02-V-752, S02-V-602, S02-V-893, S02-V-895), is CM-MKS-005's. Cross-cutting, a reading: every amount in every area names a currency.

subject: S-02
question: who sets "currency"
reading: A reading: the seller, and on BigCommerce and WooCommerce the buyer choosing among the seller's currencies (S02-V-976, S02-V-898), set the platform's own currency settings, CM-MKS-006's per market and CM-MKS-005's for the store: core, not a conflict. The third parties named, the enabled payment gateway and partners on Zid (S02-V-757, S02-V-758) and Stripe on BigCommerce (S02-V-814), convert amounts, which is CM-MKS-007's thing alone, so it is named for them.

subject: S-02
question: what "languages" takes its value per
reading: A reading: the store's languages, per market on Salla, Shopify and BigCommerce (per sales channel) and one list for the store on Zid and WooCommerce, are CM-MKS-008's thing, store languages and translation, whose note says a market's languages may be set there.
conflict: count (rows: S02-E1, model): WooCommerce: the subject's S02-WC-423 (WC_Email::setup_locale(), 'Set the locale to the store locale for customer emails to make sure emails are in the store language') is WooCommerce's own code using the store's language, a built-in behaviour the model's rules place core, and S02-WC-325 ('the shop displays in your locale if the language file exists') reads the same way; CM-MKS-008's WooCommerce cell is none-held (searched translation;translate;multilingual;language;languages;locale;i18n;localization;localisation). A reading: the statements bear out core for the store's language in WooCommerce's own behaviour, while the setting itself sits in WordPress's admin (S02-WC-324, which the model's practice reads as shows, as CM-STF-002 cites WC-C-080/decides/WC-S-0884) and WordPress fetches the translation (S02-WC-326, outside at most); the coordinator's amendment citing S02-WC-423 would settle it | placement (rows: S02-F10, model): BigCommerce: the subject's S02-BC-287 (S02-V-986) shows PayPal translating many of its payment methods by the shopper's location, a third party doing part of the translation, while CM-MKS-008's BigCommerce cell is core (BC-C-048/decides/BC-S-0271, BC-C-048/decides/BC-S-0272) and places no one outside. A reading: the same statement shows BigCommerce translating payment methods itself, and PayPal only its own methods' labels, a provider's own content; whether a provider's labels are the capability's thing (the store's content) would settle whether an outside placement is owed
outcome: model amended: E-woocommerce/evidence.tsv CM-MKS-008 woocommerce, core on S02-WC-423 (its own code sets customer emails to the store's locale), shows S02-WC-325; the count up by one (the coordinator) | dismissed: PayPal translates its own payment methods' labels beside BigCommerce's own translation (S02-BC-287); that is PayPal's interface, not the store's languages, so the cell's core stands (the coordinator)

subject: S-02
question: who sets "language"
reading: A reading: who sets the store's languages: the seller, on Shopify and BigCommerce the platform's default, on Zid the buyer through the Region & Language popup, on BigCommerce a staff permission: each the platform's own setting in CM-MKS-008, core. The third parties named, PayPal on BigCommerce and WordPress on WooCommerce, translate, CM-MKS-008's thing too.

subject: S-02
question: what "domains" takes its value per
reading: A reading: the store's domains, one active at a time on Zid (S02-V-761) and connected in Settings > Domains on Shopify (S02-V-612), are CM-SFR-008's thing; a market's own domain or subdomain (Salla S02-V-682, Shopify S02-V-611, BigCommerce per storefront S02-V-818) is CM-MKS-004's, a market's local domain (Shopify's MarketWebPresence).

subject: S-02
question: who sets "domains"
reading: A reading: who sets a domain: the seller on all four that hold it, the platform's default link and a staff permission on Zid (S02-V-1064, S02-V-1065): each the platform's own setting, CM-SFR-008's for the store's domains and CM-MKS-004's for a market's (found with caps on its MarketWebPresence cell), core. subject: S-02
question: what "product availability" takes its value per
reading: A reading: the question is which products a store offers, per market. Its main thing is CM-B2B-003, product lists assigned to markets, where Shopify's catalogs sit ('Catalogs determine which products are available in each market', S02-V-614) and whose note says they serve region markets; the platforms also answer in capabilities of their own: BigCommerce's products assigned to storefront channels (S02-V-820) in CM-CHN-001, WooCommerce's products listed on Google by their channel visibility under Google for WooCommerce (S02-V-904, S02-WC-356) in CM-CHN-004, Shopify's products hidden by country under Managed Markets (S02-V-615, S02-V-616) in CM-MKS-003, Zid's products shown by the customer's city (S02-V-764) in CM-INV-010, WooCommerce's product hidden from POS mode (S02-V-904) in CM-POS-001, and Salla's order of products within each category per market (S02-V-684, S02-V-685) in CM-CAT-003. WooCommerce's catalog visibility (S02-V-1083) is a product's own field, not landed apart.
conflict: count (rows: S02-D6, S02-E1, model): Salla and Zid: the subject's statements show each platform's own per-market product lists, Salla's product page field Product Display in Markets and its markets table column (S02-SA-155, S02-SA-165, S02-SA-281) and its setting markets#auto_show_products_in_scope (S02-SA-082), and Zid's markets feature managing each market's products (S02-ZD-010, S02-ZD-019, S02-ZD-493): built-in features, core by the model's rules; CM-B2B-003's Salla cell is not-stated (SA-S-5047, wholesale prices only) and its Zid cell none-held. A reading: the statements bear out core on both; whether the model holds a market's product list in CM-B2B-003, as it holds Shopify's (SH-C-037/decides/SH-S-5102), or in each platform's Markets cell (CM-MKS-001: SA-C-165/where/SA-S-1730, ZD-C-034/where/ZD-S-0748) would settle where the amendment goes
outcome: model amended: D-anchor/evidence.tsv CM-B2B-003 salla and D-zid/evidence.tsv CM-B2B-003 zid, core on their per-market product lists, as Shopify's market catalogs; the count up by two (the coordinator)

subject: S-02
question: who sets "product availability"
reading: A reading: who sets a market's products: the seller on all five, with Shopify's catalog permissions (S02-V-1057, S02-V-1059), Salla's option to add new products to selected markets (S02-V-687), Zid's location display off by default (S02-V-1091) and WooCommerce's Google channel visibility and POS visibility, on by default (S02-V-905, S02-V-1005): each the platform's own setting, core, in the capabilities S02-VP-47 lands on. Shopify's automatic HS classification and country restrictions (S02-V-619) are Managed Markets', CM-MKS-003. No third party is named as setting it.

subject: S-02
question: what "pricing" takes its value per
reading: A reading: the question is what a product's price takes its value per. Prices set per market or storefront (Shopify's catalogs S02-V-620, Salla S02-V-688, Zid S02-V-766, BigCommerce's price lists per channel S02-V-822) are CM-B2B-003's thing, price lists assigned to markets, channels or customer groups; prices converted at the market's exchange rate are CM-MKS-007's, and WooCommerce's prices shown in the buyer's currency (S02-V-906) CM-MKS-006's. BigCommerce's prices localized for shoppers' regions come from its Tax Settings API (S02-V-823, S02-BC-058), CM-TAX-001's.
conflict: count (rows: S02-D7, S02-E1, model): Salla and Zid: the subject's statements show each platform's own per-market prices, Salla's markets/product_prices option fixed, 'Set product prices manually for each market from the product page' (S02-SA-078, with S02-SA-024), and Zid's price per market and channel (S02-ZD-011), its market setup's pricing steps (S02-ZD-020, S02-ZD-021) and its Settings > Markets, 'Set different product prices for each market and customer type, including B2B pricing' (S02-ZD-489): built-in settings, core by the model's rules; CM-B2B-003's Salla cell is not-stated (SA-S-5047) and its Zid cell none-held. A reading: the statements bear out core on both; the same Salla setting's automatic option is already cited in CM-MKS-007 (SA-C-163/decides/SA-S-0117), so whether a market's own prices belong in CM-B2B-003 or in the Markets cells (CM-MKS-001) would settle where the amendment goes
outcome: model amended: D-anchor/evidence.tsv CM-B2B-003 salla and D-zid/evidence.tsv CM-B2B-003 zid, core on their per-market prices, with S02-VP-47's (the coordinator)

subject: S-02
question: who sets "pricing"
reading: A reading: who sets prices: the seller on all five, with Shopify's catalog permissions (S02-V-1058, S02-V-1060), in CM-B2B-003; the platform where the seller picks automatic conversion (Salla S02-V-690, Zid S02-V-768, WooCommerce's rounding of converted prices under WooPayments S02-V-907), CM-MKS-007's; each the platform's own setting, core. The one third party named, Global-e, whose pricing configurations 'can only be edited by Global-e' (S02-V-623, S02-SH-290), does it under Managed Markets, CM-MKS-003's thing (found with caps), whose Shopify cell already places Global-e outside (SH-C-110/where/SH-S-0561, features powered by Global-e).

subject: S-02
question: what "Discounts and gift cards" takes its value per
reading: A reading: the question is what a store's discounts, coupons and gift cards take their value per. Offers and discounts per market or storefront (Shopify S02-V-624, Salla's offer priority and number per market S02-V-691, Zid S02-V-769, BigCommerce's localized promotions S02-V-825) are CM-MKT-001's thing; coupons, per market on Salla and per channel on WooCommerce (S02-V-692, S02-V-909, S02-V-1012), CM-MKT-002's; Shopify's gift cards across markets in the store's currency (S02-V-625) CM-LOY-002's; and Salla's gifting, offered in the store's country or the market it is on in (S02-V-693, S02-SA-276), is CM-LOY-006's (found with caps).

subject: S-02
question: who sets "discounts"
reading: A reading: who sets discounts: the seller on all five (Shopify S02-V-626, Salla's coupon assigned to a market S02-V-695, Zid S02-V-770, BigCommerce S02-V-826), and on WooCommerce an administrator or shop manager (S02-V-1009), the buyer entering a code (S02-V-1010) and coupons on by default (S02-V-1011): each the platform's own discount or coupon setting, CM-MKT-001's and CM-MKT-002's, core. No third party is named.

subject: S-02
question: what "theme content" takes its value per
reading: A reading: the question is what the storefront's theme and its content take their value per: a theme per market or a market's copy of the main theme (Shopify S02-V-627, Salla S02-V-696, Zid S02-V-771, BigCommerce per storefront S02-V-827), one published theme or site-wide options for the store (S02-V-628, S02-V-911), and on Zid the customization shown by the buyer's country (S02-V-772): CM-SFR-001's thing, the online store and its theme, with its customization in CM-SFR-002, the theme editor (found with caps).

subject: S-02
question: who sets "theme content"
reading: A reading: who sets theme content: the seller on all five, a market taking the main theme by default on Salla (S02-V-698), BigCommerce's Edit Channels and Store Design permissions (S02-V-982): the platform's own settings in CM-SFR-001 and CM-SFR-002, core. Shopify's hreflang tags, generated by the platform from the market and language configuration (S02-V-630, S02-SH-174), are CM-CNT-007's, SEO, whose Shopify cell cites MarketWebPresence (found with caps).
